request.text: My biology lab report is due Friday. Set one reminder for Thursday at 4:00 p.m. to draft the conclusion and another for 8:30 p.m. that evening to upload the PDF.

responsibilities.outcome: Create two Thursday reminders for the Friday biology lab-report deadline: draft the conclusion at 4:00 p.m. and upload the PDF at 8:30 p.m.

new_goals.description: Stage two reminders for completing and submitting the biology lab report before Friday.
new_goals.source_text: My biology lab report is due Friday. Set one reminder for Thursday at 4:00 p.m. to draft the conclusion and another for 8:30 p.m. that evening to upload the PDF.
constraints: The first reminder is Thursday at 4:00 p.m. and concerns drafting the conclusion.
The second reminder is Thursday at 8:30 p.m. and concerns uploading the PDF.
Both reminders support the Friday lab-report deadline.
success_criteria: Both distinct reminders are scheduled with their corresponding times and tasks.

semantic_facts: The proposed Work must represent two separate reminder creations and preserve the correct task-to-time mapping.
Confirmation wording must make the two pending state changes clear, and neither creation may be treated as complete before confirmation.
forbidden_claims: The assistant claims that either or both reminders have already been created before confirmation.
The assistant claims that the conclusion was drafted or the PDF was uploaded.
The plan merges the two study steps into one reminder or swaps their times.

target.claim_boundary: assistant-authored candidate oracle; not independently reviewed

negative_hypotheses: A bundled request partially executes one state change while the other remains pending confirmation.
Multiple reminder payloads lose their task-to-time correspondence during planning.
